instruction_text: Speak directly to one listener with warmth and a smile in your voice; calm, steady and reassuring, like a favorite morning radio host, while keeping the news clear and credible.
asr_text: I want my daughter's high school to keep the phones. Collect them all in the morning. Give them back when school lets out. Until then, they stay with the school. Then I wouldn't be the only bad guy. We agreed she'd put her phone in a basket in the living room at night. My daughter didn't keep that promise, so I took her phone away. The next morning, breakfast was quiet. I could hear only dishes. I wanted her to keep our agreement, but after taking her phone, I couldn't look her in the face. I don't want another morning like that. It would help if I could say the school did it too. I'm tired of arguing every night. But really, I just want to push this onto the school. At work, I'm the one who makes the arrangements. At home, I want to get out of being the bad guy. I'm a dad, asking the school to come to my rescue.
